minutes.headline: Personnel Committee kept re-rating job descriptions for the pay grid and approved step two for one executive assistant hire.
minutes.summary: The committee spent nearly the whole meeting going through its classification outliers, position by position, adjusting degree ratings and resulting rubric grades for facilities, building, COA, library, beach, recreation, clerks, assistants, treasurer, assessor and others. It also voted by roll call on a step placement for a planning assistant moving to executive assistant to the town manager and select board. Members voiced concern about transparency and about positions paid below average, and set the next meeting for Wednesday the 21st.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none was offered.
Chair checked again for public comment before scheduling; the only person named on Zoom was Pauline, and no comment is captured.

votes.motion: Approve step two placement for the administrative assistant in planning moving to executive assistant to the town manager and select board, by roll call.
Adjourn at 7:40 pm, by roll call.

budget_items.topic: Warrant article / town meeting number for classification and pay
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said a number for the warrant article must be provided and reviewed by the town manager before the March 18th warrant, and urged moving on to the grid.
A member reported work on the FY24 grid and a step-plus-one scenario to learn the dollar cost per hour to the town, to be reviewed together rather than emailed.

A member noted that nearly all positions sit below the gathered averages and that closing the gap may need to be spread over two or three years; step one is fitting current pay into the 2024 grid, with pay equal or higher.

budget_items.topic: Step placement for new executive assistant
budget_items.what_was_said: Step two recommended given municipal experience since May and outside grant-writing and procurement experience, with a grade change from clerical union to the SAP plan.

decisions.decision: Building Commissioner judgment rating set at 80 after a note from the previous week.
Building Commissioner confidential information moved down to a two (40 points).
Building Commissioner total reaches 745, grade 11, still below land use director; members agree land use should be higher but did not resolve how.
COA director moved to grade 11 at 720 points.
Dietary aide physical demands moved to 20 and an action item taken to correct the job description lifting language.
Library page left at the grade five total after occupational hazards and physical demands discussion.
Beach director falls from grade nine to grade eight after changes; members noted the title may suggest more than the role.
Recreation director moves from rubric grade 10 to nine at 575 points.
Executive assistant to town manager and select board totals 500, rubric grade eight.
Police executive assistant totals 530, grade eight; the committee noted the position is not yet accepted at town meeting.
Treasurer/tax collector rises to 675 points, new grade 10, aligned with principal assessor.
Sewer business manager totals 620, rubric grade nine; members stressed ratings are not final until the grid is plotted.
Network administrator occupational hazards moved to 40 and personal contact to four.
Next meeting set for Wednesday the 21st at 5:00 pm, location to be confirmed; a further meeting discussed around the 26th.

what_happened.line: The committee spent most of the meeting re-rating job descriptions, position by position, to settle rubric grades for the new pay grid.
Ratings moved for several positions, including the beach director, down from grade nine to eight, and the treasurer/tax collector, up to grade 10.
A roll-call vote on step two placement for a planning assistant moving to executive assistant to the town manager and select board was taken; the result was not captured.
Members said ratings are not final until the grid is plotted, and that a warrant article number must be reviewed by the town manager before the March 18th warrant.
Next meeting was set for Wednesday the 21st at 5:00 pm, with a further meeting discussed around the 26th.

why_it_matters: The grades set here decide where each town job lands on the pay grid, which sets the town's payroll cost and the amount a classification and pay article on the March town meeting warrant would ask voters to approve.
